The problem is changing which elements are present without a second container. Elements sit back to back, so removing one from the middle means every element after it must shift down to close the gap, O(n) for one removal and O(n²) repeated once per element. Copying only the kept elements into a new container avoids the shifting but pays O(n) extra space for a layout you already had.

fixes both: one index reads every element once, and a second names the next slot for an element that stays, copying into it and advancing both indices when the current element should stay, or only moving the reading index on when it should not. The invariant, true before and after every step, is that every slot before the write index already holds the kept elements in their original order, and because it never gets ahead of the reading index, a copy never overwrites something unread.
